title: Greeting to the Church in Philadelphia
english: Ignatius, who is also called Theophorus, to the church of God the Father and of the Lord Jesus Christ at Philadelphia in Asia. This church has received mercy and is established in the concord of God. It rejoices without doubting in the passion of our Lord, and through his resurrection it has been fully assured of every mercy. I greet this church in the blood of Jesus Christ, which is eternal and abiding joy, especially if they are of one mind with the bishop and with the council of elders and the deacons who have been appointed alongside him according to the purpose of Jesus Christ. He established these leaders in firmness by his Holy Spirit according to his own will.
orientation: Ignatius opens his letter to the church in Philadelphia, greeting them as a church established in God's concord and rejoicing in Christ's passion and resurrection.

title: The bishop's ministry is from God, not from himself
english: I have come to know this bishop, and I am certain that he did not receive his ministry for the common good from himself or through human beings, nor out of vainglory, but in the love of God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ. I am astonished at his gentleness: though he is silent, he has more power than those who speak empty words.

For he is attuned to the commandments like strings on a lyre. That is why my soul blesses his disposition toward God, for I have recognized that it is virtuous and perfect: his steadfastness and his freedom from anger, all in the gentleness of the living God.
orientation: Ignatius is praising the bishop of Philadelphia, whom he has met, and explaining why the bishop's quiet gentleness is powerful.

title: Flee division; follow the shepherd
english: So then, children of the light of truth, flee from division and from evil teachings. Where the shepherd is, there follow as sheep.
For many wolves, seemingly trustworthy, take captive the runners for God with evil pleasure; but in your unity they will have no place.
orientation: Ignatius is writing to the church in Philadelphia, urging them to avoid division and false teaching by staying united around their shepherd.

title: Stay away from false teachers and follow the bishop
english: Keep away from the evil plants, which Jesus Christ does not cultivate, because they are not the Father's planting. I did not find division among you, but a filtering out of what is false.
For all who belong to God and Jesus Christ are with the bishop. And all who repent and come to the unity of the church will also belong to God, so that they may live according to Jesus Christ.

Do not be deceived, my brothers and sisters: if anyone follows one who makes a division, that person does not inherit the kingdom of God. If anyone follows someone else's teaching, that person does not share in the passion.
orientation: Ignatius is writing to the church in Philadelphia, warning them to avoid false teachers and to remain united with their bishop.

title: One Eucharist, one flesh, one altar
english: Make every effort, then, to share in one Eucharist. For there is one flesh of our Lord Jesus Christ and one cup that unites us in his blood, one altar, just as there is one bishop together with the council of elders and the deacons, my fellow servants. Do this so that whatever you do, you may act according to God.
orientation: Ignatius is urging the Philadelphians to unite around the bishop and the single Eucharist, continuing his warning against division.

title: The Prophets and Apostles as One Hope in Christ
english: My brothers and sisters, I am utterly poured out in love for you, and with overflowing joy I am working to make you secure. Yet it is not I who do this, but Jesus Christ. Because I am still bound in him, I am all the more afraid, since I am still incomplete. But your prayer to God will complete me, so that I may attain the lot in which I was shown mercy. I have taken refuge in the gospel as in the flesh of Jesus, and in the apostles as in the council of elders of the church.

We also love the prophets, because they too announced the gospel beforehand, hoped in him, and waited for him. By believing in him they were saved, being in the unity of Jesus Christ. They are saints worthy of love and worthy of wonder, witnessed to by Jesus Christ and numbered together in the gospel of our common hope.
orientation: Ignatius, bishop of Antioch, is writing to the church in Philadelphia while being taken under guard to Rome, and here he speaks of his own incompleteness and the unity of prophets and apostles in the gospel.

title: Reject Judaizing teaching and the ruler of this age
english: If anyone interprets Judaism for you, do not listen to him. It is better to hear Christianity from a man who has been circumcised than to hear Judaism from a man who has not. But if neither of them speaks about Jesus Christ, then to me they are tombstones and graves of the dead, on which only the names of human beings are written.

Flee, then, from the evil crafts and the snares of the ruler of this age, so that you may never be oppressed by his purpose and grow weak in love. Instead, all of you come together with an undivided heart.

I thank my God that I have a good conscience among you, and no one can boast, either secretly or openly, that I burdened anyone in small things or in great things. And for all those to whom I spoke, I pray that my words may not become testimony against them.
orientation: Ignatius is writing to the church in Philadelphia, warning them against false teachers and urging unity.

title: The Spirit's cry for unity around the bishop
english: Even if some people wanted to deceive me in the flesh, the Spirit is not deceived, because the Spirit is from God. For the Spirit knows where it comes from and where it is going, and it exposes hidden things. I cried out while I was among you. I spoke with a loud voice, with God's voice: "Pay attention to the bishop and to the council of elders and to the deacons."

Some of you suspected that I said these things because I knew in advance about the division of certain people. But the one in whom I am bound is my witness that I did not learn it from human flesh. The Spirit was proclaiming, saying these things: "Do nothing without the bishop. Keep your flesh as a temple of God. Love unity. Flee divisions. Become imitators of Jesus Christ, as also he is of his Father."
orientation: Ignatius is writing to the Philadelphians, recounting how he cried out with a divine voice among them, urging unity with the bishop, elders, and deacons.

title: The true archives are Christ's cross, death, and resurrection
english: For my part, I was doing what belonged to me as a person fitted for unity. But where there is division and anger, God does not dwell. The Lord forgives all who repent, if they repent into the unity of God and the council of elders under the bishop. I trust in the grace of Jesus Christ, who will release every bond from you.

I urge you to do nothing out of rivalry, but according to the teaching of Christ. For I heard some people saying, "Unless I find it in the ancient records, I do not believe it in the gospel." And when I said to them, "It is written," they answered me, "That is disputed." But for me, the ancient records are Jesus Christ; the inviolable ancient records are his cross and his death and his resurrection and the faith that is through him. In these I want to be justified through your prayer.
orientation: Ignatius is writing to the Philadelphians, urging them to repent into unity with God and the bishop's council, and answering those who demand proof from the archives.

title: The gospel surpasses the priests
english: The priests are good, but the high priest is greater. He is the one entrusted with the Holy of Holies, and he alone is entrusted with the hidden things of God. He is the door of the Father, and through him Abraham and Isaac and Jacob and the prophets and the apostles and the church all enter. All these things lead into the unity of God.

The gospel has something exceptional: the coming of our Savior, the Lord Jesus Christ, his passion, and his resurrection. The beloved prophets proclaimed these things, pointing to him. But the gospel is the completion of incorruption. Everything together is good, if you believe in love.
orientation: Ignatius is writing to the church in Philadelphia, urging unity around the bishop and contrasting the old authorities with the gospel of Jesus Christ.

title: Send a deacon to Antioch to rejoice with the church at peace
english: I have received word that the church in Antioch of Syria is at peace, because of your prayers and the compassion you have in Christ Jesus. It is fitting for you, as a church of God, to appoint a deacon to go there as God's envoy, so that he may rejoice with them when they have gathered together and glorify the name.

Blessed in Jesus Christ is the one who will be deemed worthy of such a ministry, and you will be glorified. If you want to do this, it is not impossible for you for the sake of God's name, just as the nearest churches sent bishops, and others sent elders and deacons.
orientation: Ignatius is writing to the church in Smyrna, urging them to send a representative to the church in Antioch, which is now at peace.

title: Commendation of Philo and Rheus Agathopus, and greetings from Troas
english: Now about Philo, the deacon from Cilicia. He is a man of attested character, and even now he serves me in the word of God together with Rheus Agathopus, a chosen man who has followed me from Syria after renouncing his former life. Both of them bear witness to you, and I thank God on your behalf because you welcomed them as the Lord welcomed you. As for those who dishonored them, may they be redeemed in the grace of Jesus Christ.

The love of the brothers and sisters in Troas greets you. It is from there that I am writing to you through Burrhus, who was sent with me by the Ephesians and Smyrnaeans as a mark of honor. The Lord Jesus Christ will honor them, for in him they hope with flesh, soul, spirit, faith, love, and concord. Farewell in Christ Jesus, our common hope.
orientation: Ignatius is closing his letter to the Smyrnaeans, commending two companions who have served him and sending greetings from the brothers in Troas.
